tax.text: See "Application of Critical Accounting Policies" included later in this Item 7 for additional information about our provision for income taxes. A reconciliation of the statutory U.S. federal tax rate to our effective tax rate is set forth in Item 8 under Note 10, "Income Taxes" in the Notes to Consolidated and Combined Financial Statements.

net.text: In 2025, equity increased $185.0 million as a result of net income attributable to common shareholders of $145.1 million, the impact of equity-based awards and related settlement activities of $9.8 million, currency translation adjustment of $72.2 million, and changes in pension and postretirement plan assets and benefit obligations, net of tax of $0.5 million. These increases were partially offset by cash dividends of $39.0 million, and noncontrolling interest of acquired entity of $3.6 million.

ocf.heading: Operating Activities
ocf.text: Cash provided by operating activities was $241.5 million in 2025, compared with $214.1 million in 2024. The increase in cash provided by operating activities was primarily driven by improved working capital management.

sbc.text: Equity investment loss increased by $12.3 million in 2025 compared with 2024 driven by stock-based compensation issued to senior management of Antares Vision, as a result of acquiring a 32.3% equity interest in the fourth quarter of 2025. See Note 3 “Acquisitions”

wc.text: For the year ended December 31, 2025, we drew $406.5 million and repaid $490.5 million on our Revolving Facility to fund working capital requirements. We also drew £300.0 million, or $400.4 million, on the Term Loan A to fund the DLR acquisition and repaid $40.9 million.

capex.text: Cash used for investing activities primarily consists of cash used for capital expenditures and acquisitions. Capital expenditures are made primarily for increasing capacity, replacing equipment, supporting new product development, and improving information systems. We expect capital expenditures of approximately $75 million to $80 million in 2026.

lines.why: Cash can repay debt or be paid out: a financial asset. Cash needed to run the business is operating; move it if you know how much.

lines.name: Receivables
lines.why: Owed by customers for sales: operating.

lines.name: Inventory
lines.why: Goods held for sale: operating.

lines.name: Prepaid and other current assets
lines.why: Prepayments and other operating items: operating.

lines.name: Property, plant and equipment
lines.why: Assets used to produce and sell: operating.

lines.name: Operating lease right-of-use assets
lines.why: Leased stores, offices and equipment used in the business: operating.

lines.name: Goodwill
lines.why: Paid for acquired businesses: operating.

lines.name: Intangible assets
lines.why: Acquired technology, brands and customer relationships: operating.

lines.name: Deferred tax assets
lines.why: Taxes on operating income paid ahead: operating.

lines.name: Other non-current assets
lines.why: Other long-term operating items: operating.

lines.name: Accounts payable
lines.why: Owed to suppliers for operations: operating.

lines.name: Accrued liabilities
lines.why: Services and other costs not yet paid: operating.

lines.name: Accrued compensation
lines.why: Wages, bonuses and benefits earned but not yet paid: operating.

lines.name: Deferred revenue
lines.why: Customers' payments ahead of delivery: operating.

lines.name: Income taxes payable
lines.why: Taxes on operating income: operating.

lines.name: Short-term debt and commercial paper
lines.why: Borrowed money: financial.

lines.name: Long-term debt
lines.why: Bonds, notes and loans: financial.

lines.name: Operating lease liabilities
lines.why: Rent owed on leases used in the business: operating by default. Move it to financing to treat leases like debt (if the balance sheet has no lease line of its own, they sit inside other liabilities).

lines.name: Income taxes payable, non-current
lines.why: Taxes on operating income due after a year (often uncertain tax positions): operating.

lines.name: Deferred tax liabilities
lines.why: Taxes on operating income deferred: operating.

lines.name: Pension and retiree benefits
lines.why: Promised to employees for their work: operating (some analysts treat the unfunded part as debt).

lines.name: Deferred revenue, non-current
lines.why: Customers' payments for later years: operating.

lines.name: Other non-current liabilities
lines.why: Other long-term operating obligations: operating.

lines.name: Other current assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total current assets minus the current lines above: current assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other non-current assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Non-current assets (total assets − current assets) minus the non-current lines above: assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other current liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total current liabilities minus the current lines above: current liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other non-current liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Non-current liabilities (total liabilities − current liabilities) minus the non-current lines above: liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

Our revenues depend on numerous unpredictable factors, including changes in market demand, general economic conditions, customer capital spending, timing and amount of contract awards and credit availability.
In addition, w e rely on single or sole‑source suppliers for certain critical materials and components.
We rely on a combination of trade secrets, patents, trademarks, copyrights and confidentiality practices to protect our products and technology.

Because many of our products are sophisticated and complex and may incorporate or rely on third‑party hardware, software, and data, notwithstanding testing and quality control, defects or errors may still occur.
(b) Variable interest payments are excluded because the underlying interest rates will depend on changes in market-based rates and cannot be reasonably estimated.
The primary source of the cash on hand as of the date of Separation was due to a transfer from Holdings to us as part of the Separation.
Cash contributions in subsequent years will depend on several factors including the investment performance of plan assets for funded plans.

(a) Determination of U.S. income taxes and non-U.S. withholding taxes due upon repatriation of this $ 679.6 million of earnings is not practicable because the amount of such taxes depends upon circumstances existing in numerous taxing jurisdictions at the time the remittance occurs.

Noncash consideration for equity method investment

s.t: Equity investment loss increased by $12.3 million in 2025 compared with 2024 driven by stock-based compensation issued to senior management of Antares Vision, as a result of acquiring a 32.3% equity interest in the fourth quarter of 2025.

Upon completion of the mandatory tender offer Crane NXT will implement steps aimed at delisting Antares Vision and acquire the remaining stake owned by Regolo S.p.A. As a result of the transaction, Antares Vision will become a subsidiary of Crane NXT.

The Company accounts for its investment in Antares Vision in the first phase under equity method accounting since it exercises significant influence over Antares Vision, but does not have a controlling financial interest.
